entities.name: Angelo Capranica
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Angelo Capranica was a prominent Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a crucial role in the High Middle Ages. Born into a noble family, he rose to prominence through his education and clerical appointments, eventually becoming a cardinal in 1456. During his tenure as cardinal, he participated in several conclaves that elected popes, including Pius II, who later became Pope EII. Capranica's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he collaborated with European monarchs and nobles on matters of state and church politics.

As a key figure in the Catholic Church during this period, Capranica contributed to the development of papal authority and the growth of urban centers in Italy. His legacy can be seen in the numerous churches and monasteries he founded or renovated, which continue to stand as testaments to his devotion to Christianity.

Despite his significant influence, Capranica's life was cut short when he died in 1478 at the age of approximately 100. His remarkable life and achievements serve as a testament to the enduring power of faith and leadership during the medieval period.
